tasks.title: Layers 1–2: a switch port is off
tasks.statement: PC 1 and PC 2 are connected to the switch, and the addresses are configured correctly. But PC 2 is unreachable. Run ping and look at the log: the frame reaches the switch and has nowhere to go from there. Select the switch and look at its ports.
tasks.hint: The switch card has a list of ports with checkboxes. The port that PC 2 is plugged into is off. In the switch terminal the commands are `show ports` and `port p2 up`.

tasks.title: Layer 3: wrong mask
tasks.statement: Two computers on the same network 192.168.0.0/24 are connected through a switch. PC 1 sends a request and gets no reply. Check the log: PC 2 receives the packet but cannot reply, because by its settings the address of PC 1 is “not on its network”, and it has no gateway. Find the mistake in the PC 2 settings.
tasks.hint: The PC 2 mask is /25, which covers only the addresses .0–.127, while PC 2 itself has the address .200. Set /24. Edit the mask field in the card and press Enter.

tasks.title: Layer 4: nobody listens on the port
tasks.statement: The PC pings the server without problems, but cannot connect to port 80: an RST comes back. The network is fine, the problem is at the transport layer. Start listening on port 80 on the server: open the server card and add the port, or type `nc -l 80` in the terminal.
tasks.hint: The server itself replies with RST when the port is closed. As soon as the port is listening, a SYN-ACK will arrive.

spec_text./goals/1/text: The PC connects to port 80 on the server

tasks.title: Layer 4: a firewall blocks the port
tasks.statement: The server is listening on port 80, ping works, but the connection to port 80 “stays silent”: neither SYN-ACK nor RST, the packet just vanishes. There is a firewall rule on the router. Find it in the log (the line “firewall: DROP”) and delete it.
tasks.hint: Select the router: at the bottom of its card there is a “Firewall” section. The DROP rule for tcp port 80 is deleted with the cross. Ping keeps working because the rule does not affect ICMP.

tasks.title: Three faults on one path
tasks.statement: The PC has to open a page on the server through a switch and a router. There are three faults on the path, one each at the physical, network and transport layers. Work from the bottom up: ping, log, terminal. When both ping and the connection to port 80 work, the exercise is complete.
tasks.hint: Physical: the switch port for the PC is off. Network: the PC has no default gateway (192.168.1.1). Transport: the server is not listening on port 80.
